body.en: Unit 10 establishes the rigorous mathematical theory of infinite processes. Beginning with the formal (ε, N) definition of sequence limits, the unit develops the complete taxonomy of series convergence tests, proves the convergence of geometric series, and establishes the criteria for absolute versus conditional convergence.
body.ar: Unit 10 establishes the rigorous mathematical theory of infinite processes. Beginning with the formal (ε, N) definition of المتتالية النهايات, the unit develops the complete taxonomy of المتسلسلة convergence tests, proves the convergence of geometric المتسلسلة, and establishes the criteria for absolute versus conditional convergence.

blocks.heading: Level 1 · Foundations — Precise Sequence Limits & The Geometric Series Sum Proof

body.en: An infinite series \(\sum a_n\) is defined as the limit of its sequence of partial sums \(S_N = \sum_{n=1}^N a_n\). Understanding sequence convergence is the necessary prerequisite for series analysis.
body.ar: An infinite المتسلسلة \(\sum a_n\) is defined as the النهاية of its المتتالية of partial sums \(S_N = \sum_{n=1}^N a_n\). Understanding المتتالية convergence is the necessary prerequisite for المتسلسلة analysis.

label.en: ● Theorem & Formal Analytical Proof · Geometric Series Sum Formula
label.ar: ● مبرهنة & Formal Analytical برهان · Geometric المتسلسلة Sum الصيغة

body.en:
Theorem: The geometric series \(\displaystyle\sum_{n=0}^\infty a r^n = a + ar + ar^2 + \dots\) converges if and only if \(|r| < 1\). When \(|r| < 1\), its infinite sum is: \[ S = \frac{a}{1 - r}. \] If \(|r| \ge 1\) and \(a \neq 0\), the series diverges.

Proof via Partial Sums: Consider the \(N\)-th partial sum: \[ S_N = a + ar + ar^2 + \dots + ar^{N-1}. \] Multiply both sides by the common ratio \(r\): \[ r S_N = ar + ar^2 + ar^3 + \dots + ar^N. \] Subtract the second equation from the first. All intermediate terms cancel in a telescoping subtraction: \[ S_N - r S_N = a - ar^N \implies S_N(1 - r) = a(1 - r^N). \] Since \(r \neq 1\), divide by \(1 - r\): \[ S_N = \frac{a(1 - r^N)}{1 - r}. \] Now take the limit as \(N \to \infty\): \[ S = \lim_{N\to\infty} S_N = \lim_{N\to\infty} \frac{a(1 - r^N)}{1 - r} = \frac{a}{1 - r}\left(1 - \lim_{N\to\infty} r^N\right). \] • If \(|r| < 1\), \(\lim_{N\to\infty} r^N = 0\), yielding: \[ S = \frac{a(1 - 0)}{1 - r} = \mathbf{\frac{a}{1 - r}}. \] • If \(|r| > 1\) or \(r = -1\), \(\lim_{N\to\infty} r^N\) does not exist (diverges).
• If \(r = 1\), \(S_N = N a \to \pm\infty\) as \(N \to \infty\). \(\blacksquare\)
body.ar:
Theorem: The geometric المتسلسلة \(\displaystyle\sum_{n=0}^\infty a r^n = a + ar + ar^2 + \dots\) converges if and only if \(|r| < 1\). عندما \(|r| < 1\), its infinite sum is: \[ S = \frac{a}{1 - r}. \] If \(|r| \ge 1\) and \(a \neq 0\), the المتسلسلة diverges.

Proof via Partial Sums: Consider the \(N\)-th partial sum: \[ S_N = a + ar + ar^2 + \dots + ar^{N-1}. \] Multiply both sides by the common ratio \(r\): \[ r S_N = ar + ar^2 + ar^3 + \dots + ar^N. \] Subtract the second المعادلة from the first. All intermediate terms cancel in a telescoping subtraction: \[ S_N - r S_N = a - ar^N \implies S_N(1 - r) = a(1 - r^N). \] Since \(r \neq 1\), divide by \(1 - r\): \[ S_N = \frac{a(1 - r^N)}{1 - r}. \] Now take the النهاية as \(N \to \infty\): \[ S = \lim_{N\to\infty} S_N = \lim_{N\to\infty} \frac{a(1 - r^N)}{1 - r} = \frac{a}{1 - r}\left(1 - \lim_{N\to\infty} r^N\right). \] • If \(|r| < 1\), \(\lim_{N\to\infty} r^N = 0\), yielding: \[ S = \frac{a(1 - 0)}{1 - r} = \mathbf{\frac{a}{1 - r}}. \] • If \(|r| > 1\) or \(r = -1\), \(\lim_{N\to\infty} r^N\) does not exist (diverges).
• If \(r = 1\), \(S_N = N a \to \pm\infty\) as \(N \to \infty\). \(\blacksquare\)

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Unit 10 · Infinite Sequences & Series — Convergence Tests)
label.ar: ◆ لماذا تعمل هذه الطريقة رياضياً — First-Principles اشتقاق (Unit 10 · Infinite المتتاليات & المتسلسلة — Convergence Tests)

body.en:
Why the Geometric Sum Formula & \(S_\infty\) Work: Write \(S_n = a + ar + ar^2 + \dots + ar^{n-1}\). Multiplying through by \(r\) shifts every power up by one:

\[ S_n - rS_n = (a + ar + \dots + ar^{n-1}) - (ar + ar^2 + \dots + ar^n) = a - ar^n \]

Factoring \(S_n(1 - r) = a(1 - r^n)\) gives \(S_n = \dfrac{a(1 - r^n)}{1 - r}\) for \(r \ne 1\). Taking \(n \to \infty\), \(\lim_{n \to \infty} r^n = 0\) holds if and only if \(|r| < 1\), yielding \(S_\infty = \dfrac{a}{1 - r}\).
body.ar:
Why the Geometric Sum الصيغة & \(S_\infty\) Work: Write \(S_n = a + ar + ar^2 + \dots + ar^{n-1}\). Multiplying through by \(r\) shifts every power up by one:

\[ S_n - rS_n = (a + ar + \dots + ar^{n-1}) - (ar + ar^2 + \dots + ar^n) = a - ar^n \]

Factoring \(S_n(1 - r) = a(1 - r^n)\) gives \(S_n = \dfrac{a(1 - r^n)}{1 - r}\) for \(r \ne 1\). Taking \(n \to \infty\), \(\lim_{n \to \infty} r^n = 0\) holds if and only if \(|r| < 1\), yielding \(S_\infty = \dfrac{a}{1 - r}\).

label.en: Level 1 (Foundations) — Worked Example · Geometric Series Identification & Sum
label.ar: Level 1 (Foundations) — مثال محلول · Geometric المتسلسلة Identification & Sum

body.en:
Problem: Determine whether the series \(\sum_{n=1}^\infty 5\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)^n\) converges or diverges. If it converges, compute its exact sum.

Step 1 · Identify First Term \(a\) and Common Ratio \(r\):
• For \(n = 1\): \(a_1 = 5\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)^1 = -\frac{10}{3}\).
• The common ratio is \(r = -\frac{2}{3}\).

Step 2 · Convergence Test: \[ |r| = \left|-\frac{2}{3}\right| = \frac{2}{3} < 1. \] Since \(|r| < 1\), the geometric series converges.

Step 3 · Calculate Sum: \[ S = \frac{a_1}{1 - r} = \frac{-10/3}{1 - (-2/3)} = \frac{-10/3}{5/3} = -\frac{10}{3} \cdot \frac{3}{5} = \mathbf{-2}. \]
body.ar:
Problem: حدّد ما إذا كان the المتسلسلة \(\sum_{n=1}^\infty 5\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)^n\) converges or diverges. If it converges, compute its exact sum.

Step 1 · Identify First Term \(a\) and Common Ratio \(r\):
• For \(n = 1\): \(a_1 = 5\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)^1 = -\frac{10}{3}\).
• The common ratio is \(r = -\frac{2}{3}\).

Step 2 · Convergence Test: \[ |r| = \left|-\frac{2}{3}\right| = \frac{2}{3} < 1. \] Since \(|r| < 1\), the geometric المتسلسلة converges.

Step 3 · احسب Sum: \[ S = \frac{a_1}{1 - r} = \frac{-10/3}{1 - (-2/3)} = \frac{-10/3}{5/3} = -\frac{10}{3} \cdot \frac{3}{5} = \mathbf{-2}. \]

label.en: Worked Example \(B\) — Unit 10 · Infinite Sequences & Series — Convergence Tests (Hard Application)
label.ar: مثال محلول \(B\) — Unit 10 · Infinite المتتاليات & المتسلسلة — Convergence Tests (Hard Application)

body.en:
Problem (Hard): Consider the sequence defined by \(a_n = \int_{0}^{1/n} \frac{\sin(x^2)}{x} dx\). Which of the following statements about the convergence of the sequence \( \{a_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty} \) is true?

Step-by-Step Solution: We need to determine the limit of the sequence \(a_n = \int_{0}^{1/n} \frac{\sin(x^2)}{x} dx\) as \(n \to \infty\). As \(n \to \infty\), the upper limit of integration \(1/n \to 0\). We examine the behavior of the integrand \(\frac{\sin(x^2)}{x}\) near \(x=0\). Using the Taylor series expansion for \(\sin(u)\) around \(u=0\), which is \(\sin(u) = u - \frac{u^3}{3!} + O(u^5)\), we substitute \(u=x^2\): \(\sin(x^2) = x^2 - \frac{(x^2)^3}{3!} + O(x^{10}) = x^2 - \frac{x^6}{6} + O(x^{10})\). Therefore, for \(x\) close to 0, \(\frac{\sin(x^2)}{x} = \frac{x^2 - \frac{x^6}{6} + O(x^{10})}{x} = x - \frac{x^5}{6} + O(x^9)\). This shows that the integrand \(\frac{\sin(x^2)}{x}\) approaches 0 as \(x \to 0\). In fact, for small \(x\), \(\frac{\sin(x^2)}{x} \approx x\), which is continuous at \(x=0\) if we define it to be 0. More formally, by L'Hopital's Rule applied to \(\frac{\sin(x^2)}{x^2}\) and then multiplying by \(x\), we can see that \(\lim_{x\to 0} \frac{\sin(x^2)}{x} = \lim_{x\to 0} x \cdot \lim_{x\to 0} \frac{\sin(x^2)}{x^2} = 0 \cdot 1 = 0\). Since the integrand is continuous on the interval \([0, 1/n]\) for any \(n \ge 1\) (if we define the integrand to be 0 at \(x=0\), or by noting the limit is 0), and the interval of integration shrinks to 0 as \(n \to \infty\), the value of the integral \(a_n\) must also approach 0. Let \(f(x) = \frac{\sin(x^2)}{x}\). For \(x \in (0, 1]\), \(f(x)\) is well-defined. As \(x \to 0^+\), \(f(x) \to 0\). We can consider a continuous extension of \(f(x)\) on \([0, 1]\) by defining \(f(0)=0\). The function \(f(x)\) is continuous on \([0, 1]\). By the Mean Value Theorem for Integrals, for \(n \ge 1\), there exists a \(c_n \in [0, 1/n]\) such that \(a_n = f(c_n) \cdot (1/n - 0) = f(c_n) \cdot (1/n)\). As \(n \to \infty\), \(c_n \to 0\). Since \(f\) is continuous at 0, \(\lim_{n \to \infty} f(c_n) = f(0) = 0\). Therefore, \(\lim_{n \to \infty} a_n = \lim_{n \to \infty} f(c_n) \cdot \frac{1}{n} = 0 \cdot 0 = 0\). Thus, the sequence converges to 0.
body.ar:
Problem (Hard): Consider the المتتالية defined by \(a_n = \int_{0}^{1/n} \frac{\sin(x^2)}{x} dx\). Which of the following statements about the convergence of the المتتالية \( \{a_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty} \) is true?

Step-by-Step الحل: We need to حدّد النهاية of the المتتالية \(a_n = \int_{0}^{1/n} \frac{\sin(x^2)}{x} dx\) as \(n \to \infty\). As \(n \to \infty\), the upper النهاية of integration \(1/n \to 0\). We examine the behavior of the integrand \(\frac{\sin(x^2)}{x}\) near \(x=0\). Using the Taylor المتسلسلة expansion for \(\sin(u)\) around \(u=0\), which is \(\sin(u) = u - \frac{u^3}{3!} + O(u^5)\), we عوّض \(u=x^2\): \(\sin(x^2) = x^2 - \frac{(x^2)^3}{3!} + O(x^{10}) = x^2 - \frac{x^6}{6} + O(x^{10})\). وبالتالي, for \(x\) close to 0, \(\frac{\sin(x^2)}{x} = \frac{x^2 - \frac{x^6}{6} + O(x^{10})}{x} = x - \frac{x^5}{6} + O(x^9)\). This shows that the integrand \(\frac{\sin(x^2)}{x}\) approaches 0 as \(x \to 0\). In fact, for small \(x\), \(\frac{\sin(x^2)}{x} \approx x\), which is continuous at \(x=0\) if we define it to be 0. More formally, by L'Hopital's Rule applied to \(\frac{\sin(x^2)}{x^2}\) and then multiplying by \(x\), we can see that \(\lim_{x\to 0} \frac{\sin(x^2)}{x} = \lim_{x\to 0} x \cdot \lim_{x\to 0} \frac{\sin(x^2)}{x^2} = 0 \cdot 1 = 0\). Since the integrand is continuous on the interval \([0, 1/n]\) for any \(n \ge 1\) (if we define the integrand to be 0 at \(x=0\), or by noting the النهاية is 0), and the interval of integration shrinks to 0 as \(n \to \infty\), the value of the التكامل \(a_n\) must also approach 0. Let \(f(x) = \frac{\sin(x^2)}{x}\). For \(x \in (0, 1]\), \(f(x)\) is well-defined. As \(x \to 0^+\), \(f(x) \to 0\). We can consider a continuous extension of \(f(x)\) on \([0, 1]\) by defining \(f(0)=0\). The الدالة \(f(x)\) is continuous on \([0, 1]\). By the Mean Value مبرهنة for التكاملات, for \(n \ge 1\), there exists a \(c_n \in [0, 1/n]\) such that \(a_n = f(c_n) \cdot (1/n - 0) = f(c_n) \cdot (1/n)\). As \(n \to \infty\), \(c_n \to 0\). Since \(f\) is continuous at 0, \(\lim_{n \to \infty} f(c_n) = f(0) = 0\). وبالتالي, \(\lim_{n \to \infty} a_n = \lim_{n \to \infty} f(c_n) \cdot \frac{1}{n} = 0 \cdot 0 = 0\). وعليه, the المتتالية converges to 0.

body.en:
1. Expanding \((a + bx)^n\) Without Factoring Out \(a^n\): For negative or fractional \(n\) on College Board AP Calculus BC, the formula \(1 + nu + \tfrac{n(n-1)}{2!}u^2 + \dots\) requires the first term inside the bracket to be 1: \((a + bx)^n = a^n\bigl(1 + \tfrac{b}{a}x\bigr)^n\). Omitting \(a^n\) loses almost all marks.

2. Confusing the \(n\)-th Term \(u_n\) with the Partial Sum \(S_n\): When given a formula for \(S_n\), extract \(u_n = S_n - S_{n-1}\) for \(n \ge 2\) and \(u_1 = S_1\).

question.en:
Level 1 · Foundations

Express the repeating decimal \(0.272727\dots = 0.\overline{27}\) as an infinite geometric series, and find its exact fraction representation in simplest form.
question.ar:
Level 1 · Foundations

Express the repeating decimal \(0.272727\dots = 0.\overline{27}\) as an infinite geometric series, and أوجد its exact fraction representation in simplest form.

solution.ar:
خطوات الحل التفصيلية:

Write as a series: \[ 0.\overline{27} = \frac{27}{100} + \frac{27}{10000} + \frac{27}{1000000} + \dots \] First term \(a = \frac{27}{100}\), common ratio \(r = \frac{1}{100}\). Since \(|r| = 0.01 < 1\): \[ S = \frac{a}{1 - r} = \frac{27/100}{1 - 1/100} = \frac{27/100}{99/100} = \frac{27}{99} = \mathbf{\frac{3}{11}}. \]

hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(0.\overline{27} = \frac{27}{100} + \frac{27}{10000} + \frac{27}{1000000} + \dots\) لتبسيط الخطوة.
تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(a = \frac{27}{100}\) ، \(r = \frac{1}{100}\) لتبسيط الخطوة.
تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(|r| = 0.01 < 1\) ، \(S = \frac{a}{1 - r} = \frac{27/100}{1 - 1/100} = \frac{27/100}{99/100} = \frac{27}{99}\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

blocks.heading: Level 2 · Medium — The Nine Series Convergence Tests Taxonomy

body.en: Every convergence problem on the AP Calculus BC exam can be resolved using one of nine standard tests. Knowing which test to apply and verifying its hypotheses is essential for scoring full justification points.
body.ar: Every convergence problem on the AP التفاضل والتكامل BC exam can be resolved using one of nine standard tests. Knowing which test to apply and verifying its hypotheses is essential for scoring full justification points.

label.ar: ● Complete Taxonomy of Convergence Tests (الوحدة ١٠ · المتتابعات والمتسلسلات اللانهائية واختبارات التقارب)

body.en:
TestForm of SeriesConvergence ConditionDivergence Condition
1. \(n\)-th Term TestAny \(\sum a_n\)Never proves convergence\(\lim a_n \neq 0\)
2. Geometric Series\(\sum a r^n\)\(|r| < 1\) (Sum: \(\frac{a}{1-r}\))\(|r| \ge 1\)
3. \(p\)-Series Test\(\sum \frac{1}{n^p}\)\(p > 1\)\(p \le 1\) (Harmonic at \(p=1\))
4. Integral Test\(a_n = f(n) > 0\), decr.\(\int_1^\infty f(x)\,dx < \infty\)\(\int_1^\infty f(x)\,dx = \infty\)
5. Direct Comparison\(0 \le a_n \le b_n\)\(\sum b_n\) converges\(a_n \ge c_n\) and \(\sum c_n\) div.
6. Limit Comparison\(a_n, b_n > 0\)\(\lim \frac{a_n}{b_n} = L \in (0, \infty)\), \(\sum b_n\) conv.\(L \in (0, \infty)\), \(\sum b_n\) div.

label.en: Level 2 (Medium) — Worked Example · Limit Comparison Test vs \(p\)-Series
label.ar: Level 2 (Medium) — مثال محلول · النهاية Comparison Test vs \(p\)-المتسلسلة

body.en:
Problem: Determine the convergence or divergence of \(\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{3n^2 + 5}{2n^4 - n + 1}\).

Step 1 · Identify Dominant Terms: For large \(n\), \(a_n \approx \frac{3n^2}{2n^4} = \frac{3}{2n^2}\). Choose benchmark series \(b_n = \frac{1}{n^2}\).

Step 2 · State Benchmark Convergence: The series \(\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{n^2}\) is a \(p\)-series with \(p = 2 > 1\), which converges.

Step 3 · Evaluate Limit of the Ratio: \[ L = \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{a_n}{b_n} = \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{\frac{3n^2 + 5}{2n^4 - n + 1}}{\frac{1}{n^2}} = \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{3n^4 + 5n^2}{2n^4 - n + 1} = \frac{3}{2}. \]

Step 4 · Conclusion & Justification: Since \(L = \frac{3}{2}\) is finite and positive (\(0 < L < \infty\)), by the Limit Comparison Test, the series \(\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{3n^2 + 5}{2n^4 - n + 1}\) converges.

question.en:
Level 2 · Medium

Apply the Ratio Test to determine the convergence or divergence of \(\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{4^n}{n!}\).
question.ar:
Level 2 · Medium

Apply the Ratio Test to حدّد convergence or divergence of \(\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{4^n}{n!}\).

solution.en: Set up the ratio: \[ \rho = \lim_{n\to\infty} \left| \frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n} \right| = \lim_{n\to\infty} \left| \frac{4^{n+1}}{(n+1)!} \cdot \frac{n!}{4^n} \right| = \lim_{n\to\infty} \left( \frac{4^{n+1}}{4^n} \cdot \frac{n!}{(n+1)n!} \right) = \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{4}{n+1} = 0. \] Since \(\rho = 0 < 1\), by the Ratio Test, the series converges absolutely.

label.en: ● Theorem & Formal Analytical Proof · Absolute Convergence Implies Convergence
label.ar: ● مبرهنة & Formal Analytical برهان · Absolute Convergence Implies Convergence

body.en:
Theorem: If \(\sum_{n=1}^\infty |a_n|\) converges, then \(\sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n\) converges.

Proof: For any real number \(a_n\), \(-|a_n| \le a_n \le |a_n|\). Adding \(|a_n|\) across all parts: \[ 0 \le a_n + |a_n| \le 2|a_n|. \] Since \(\sum |a_n|\) converges, \(\sum 2|a_n| = 2\sum |a_n|\) also converges. By the Direct Comparison Test, the series \(\sum (a_n + |a_n|)\) converges. Now express \(a_n\) as: \[ a_n = (a_n + |a_n|) - |a_n|. \] Since both \(\sum (a_n + |a_n|)\) and \(\sum |a_n|\) converge, their difference converges: \[ \sum a_n = \sum (a_n + |a_n|) - \sum |a_n|. \quad \blacksquare \]

Alternating Series Error Bound: If \(\sum_{n=1}^\infty (-1)^{n+1} a_n\) satisfies the AST conditions (\(a_n > 0\), \(a_{n+1} \le a_n\), \(\lim a_n = 0\)), then: \[ |S - S_N| \le a_{N+1}. \]

Now express \(a_n\) as: \[ a_n = (a_n + |a_n|) - |a_n|. \] Since both \(\sum (a_n + |a_n|)\) and \(\sum |a_n|\) converge, their difference converges: \[ \sum a_n = \sum (a_n + |a_n|) - \sum |a_n|. \quad \blacksquare \]

label.en: Level 3 (Advanced/FRQ) — Worked Example · Absolute vs Conditional Convergence Justification
label.ar: Level 3 (Advanced/FRQ) — مثال محلول · Absolute vs Conditional Convergence Justification

body.en:
Problem: Determine whether the alternating series \(\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{(-1)^n}{\sqrt{n}}\) converges absolutely, converges conditionally, or diverges.

Step 1 · Test Absolute Convergence: Consider the series of absolute values: \[ \sum_{n=1}^\infty \left| \frac{(-1)^n}{\sqrt{n}} \right| = \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{n^{1/2}}. \] This is a \(p\)-series with \(p = \frac{1}{2} \le 1\). Therefore, \(\sum |a_n|\) diverges. The series is NOT absolutely convergent.

Step 2 · Test the Original Alternating Series using AST: Check the three hypotheses of the Alternating Series Test:
1. Alternating sign: \((-1)^n\) oscillates signs.
2. Terms decrease in magnitude: \(a_n = \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\). Since \(n + 1 > n \implies \sqrt{n+1} > \sqrt{n} \implies \frac{1}{\sqrt{n+1}} < \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\), terms strictly decrease.
3. Limit of terms: \(\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} = 0\).

All three hypotheses hold, so by the Alternating Series Test, the series \(\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{(-1)^n}{\sqrt{n}}\) converges.

Conclusion: Because the series converges but does not converge absolutely, it converges conditionally.
body.ar:
Problem: حدّد ما إذا كان the alternating المتسلسلة \(\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{(-1)^n}{\sqrt{n}}\) converges absolutely, converges conditionally, or diverges.

Step 1 · Test Absolute Convergence: Consider the المتسلسلة of absolute values: \[ \sum_{n=1}^\infty \left| \frac{(-1)^n}{\sqrt{n}} \right| = \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{n^{1/2}}. \] This is a \(p\)-المتسلسلة with \(p = \frac{1}{2} \le 1\). وبالتالي, \(\sum |a_n|\) diverges. The المتسلسلة is NOT absolutely convergent.

Step 2 · Test the Original Alternating المتسلسلة using AST: Check the three hypotheses of the Alternating المتسلسلة Test:
1. Alternating sign: \((-1)^n\) oscillates signs.
2. Terms decrease in magnitude: \(a_n = \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\). Since \(n + 1 > n \implies \sqrt{n+1} > \sqrt{n} \implies \frac{1}{\sqrt{n+1}} < \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\), terms strictly decrease.
3. النهاية of terms: \(\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} = 0\).

All three hypotheses hold, so by the Alternating المتسلسلة Test, the المتسلسلة \(\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{(-1)^n}{\sqrt{n}}\) converges.

Conclusion: Because the المتسلسلة converges but does not converge absolutely, it converges conditionally.

question.en:
Level 3 · Advanced / AP FRQ

The alternating series \(\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{n^4}\) converges to sum \(S\). If the sum is approximated by the fourth partial sum \(S_4\), use the Alternating Series Error Bound to find an upper bound for the error \(|S - S_4|\).
question.ar:
Level 3 · Advanced / AP FRQ

The alternating series \(\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{n^4}\) converges to sum \(S\). إذا كان the sum is approximated بتطبيق fourth partial sum \(S_4\), use the Alternating Series Error Bound to أوجد an upper bound for the error \(|S - S_4|\).

solution.en: The series satisfies the hypotheses of the AST: \(a_n = \frac{1}{n^4}\) is positive, strictly decreasing, and \(\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{n^4} = 0\). By the Alternating Series Error Bound: \[ |S - S_4| \le a_5 = \frac{1}{5^4} = \frac{1}{625} = \mathbf{0.0016}. \] The approximation error is guaranteed to be less than or equal to 0.0016.
